motion.name: dur-1
motion.purpose: Colour, border and background state changes.

motion.name: dur-2
motion.purpose: Icon nudges, map hover thickening and dimming.

motion.name: dur-3
motion.purpose: Page enter, chat sheet, route transitions.

motion.name: ease-move
motion.purpose: Anything travelling along a line: draws, fills, hops, wipes.

motion.name: line-draw
motion.purpose: Map lines draw on load via stroke-dashoffset.

motion.name: packet-ride
motion.value: 7s linear infinite, two packets per line
motion.purpose: Packets travel each map line along its own path.

motion.name: station-snap
motion.value: steps(); scale 1.45 to 1 on the map, 1.5 to 1 over 220ms in runs
motion.purpose: A station fills with its line colour on arrival; stepped, never faded.

motion.name: run-hop
motion.purpose: A run advances one station at a time with Pip riding it.

motion.name: scroll-reveal
motion.value: rise 28px, opacity 620ms / transform 760ms ease-out; stagger 90ms; wipe 900ms ease-move
motion.purpose: First entry into the viewport. Hidden states gated on html.js with a 3s failsafe.

motion.name: count-up
motion.purpose: Numeric metrics count from zero when first seen.

motion.name: scroll-progress-line
motion.purpose: Four-colour reading progress under the masthead where supported.

motion.name: off-switch-reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Removes draws, packets, snaps, pulses, the progress line and reveals; runs render complete.

motion.name: off-switch-visitor-pause
motion.purpose: The visitor's pause control, remembered in localStorage; stops everything that loops.

narrative.overview:
The portfolio is a live route map. Each project is a coloured line, each stage of its real pipeline is a station on that line, and small packets ride the lines while the page is open. The visual language is that of a transit authority's public signage: a cool paper ground, near-black ink, four saturated line colours drawn as thick round-capped strokes, white stations ringed in ink, and a sturdy grotesque that changes width by role. Nothing is decorative that is not also a wayfinding device; a colour on screen always means "this belongs to that line".

The system is flat, ruled, and dense in the way a timetable is dense. Structure comes from 2px ink rules and 1px hairlines, not from boxes or shadows. Sections alternate between the paper ground and two full-bleed fields (ink and yellow), which act as the dark departures board and the terminus. Pip, the concierge robot, is a passenger in this world: it rides each pipeline run from station to station and changes mood as the visitor crosses sections.

It refuses the dark bento developer portfolio and the cream editorial folio it replaced.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper white ground, ink text, four line colours each with a darker text variant.
Lines are thick rounded strokes; stations are white circles with a heavy ink ring.
One variable grotesque (Archivo) whose width axis carries the hierarchy; one mono (Martian Mono) for figures only.
Ruled rows and boards in place of cards; corners are small (4px, 6px) or fully round.
Motion is transit motion: lines draw, packets ride, stations snap, runs hop. Everything that loops can be paused.
On phones the hero keeps a map: the three lines share a vertical trunk and peel off to the right.

rules.name: The Line Owns Its Colour Rule
rules.body: A colour is assigned by `lineFor(slug)`: red, blue and green belong to the three flagships; everything else rides yellow. A wrapper sets the line (`line-red`, `line-blue`, `line-green`, `line-yellow`) and children read `--line`, `--line-ink`, `--on-line`. Never pick a line colour by hand for visual variety.

rules.name: The Ink Variant Rule
rules.body: The line colour fills strokes, bullets and bars. Text on paper in a line's colour always uses that line's `-ink` variant. Text sitting on a line colour uses `--on-line`: white on red, blue and green; ink on yellow.

rules.name: The Two Fields Rule
rules.body: Only ink and yellow run full-bleed as section grounds. Ink is the board (Experience, footer); yellow is the last stop (contact band). Red, blue and green never become a section background.

rules.name: The Focus Follows The Ground Rule
rules.body: The focus ring is a 3px solid outline at 3px offset whose colour comes from `--focus`: blue on paper, yellow on the ink field, ink on the yellow field. Any new ground must set `--focus`.

rules.name: The Width Is The Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Width narrows as the role gets smaller: 112, 108, 106, 104 for headings, 96 for buttons, 92 for segments, 88 for signs, 82 to 85 for labels inside the map. A new text role picks a point on this scale; it does not introduce another family.

rules.name: The Mono Reads Figures Rule
rules.body: Martian Mono is for measurements, dates, times and counts. A metric whose value has no digit is set in Archivo extra-bold instead.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Signs and labels are sentence case at normal tracking. Hierarchy comes from weight and width, not from capitals or letterspacing.

rules.name: The Map Survives The Phone Rule
rules.body: Below 1024px the hero swaps to a second, purpose-drawn map: the three lines leave the interchange down one vertical trunk and peel off to the right in turn, the first to leave riding the outside edge so no two lines cross, with a thinner 9-unit stroke. It never collapses into a stack of cards.

rules.name: The Run Turns With The Screen Rule
rules.body: A pipeline run is horizontal from 640px (track across, Pip above it) and vertical below (track down the left, stations as rows, Pip at the right edge). Runs with prose under each stop draw their own segment from stop to stop on phones.

rules.name: The Only Pip Floats Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong to the concierge layer. Page content separates with rules and grounds.

dos: Do assign colour through the line: wrap in the project's line class and read `--line`, `--line-ink`, `--on-line`.
Do use the `-ink` variant whenever a line colour is used for text on paper, and ink text on yellow.
Do build lists and facts as ruled rows: 2px ink rule to open, 1px hairlines between.
Do draw stations as white circles with a heavy ink ring, and lines as round-capped bars.
Do keep corners at 4px for controls, 6px for media, or fully round; nothing in between.
Do set `--focus` on any new ground so the 3px ring stays visible.
Do give every new loop a rule under both `prefers-reduced-motion` and `html[data-motion='off']`, and gate every hidden reveal state on `html.js`.
Do keep a real map in the phone hero, using the vertical-trunk geometry.
Do set figures, dates and times in Martian Mono with tabular numerals.
donts: Don't use red, blue or green as a section background, or introduce a fifth line colour.
Don't put white text on yellow, or raw line colours on paper as text.
Don't add shadows, blur or translucent panels to page content; only the concierge floats.
Don't wrap content in rounded cards or tile grids; the board and the ruled row are the containers.
Don't fade a station; arrivals snap in steps.
Don't replace the phone map with stacked cards or hide it.
Don't add a second sans or a serif; vary Archivo's width and weight instead.
Don't return to the cream paper, warm amber and serif display of the discarded folio, or to a dark bento grid.
